nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.label: Absence effect split into pace and efficiency components
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.measurement: For each player with at least 800 minutes: on/off differences in team possessions per 48, ORtg and DRtg over 3 seasons with ridge shrinkage (k=600 possessions) and teammate adjustment (RAPM-style regression on pace as well); apply to tonight's scenario weights; as-of nightly after injury report.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.mechanism: Each rotation player's absence changes team pace and ORtg/DRtg separately, with different signs by role.
nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decompositio.rationale: The existing lineup_adj_rating collapses availability into one net rating, which is the right variable for margin but wrong for totals where a slower-and-worse offence and a faster-and-weaker defence have opposite effects.
raw_data: lineup stints with possessions and points

nba.all_star_process.label: All-Star voting/selection, captains and event participation
nba.all_star_process.measurement: Public vote leaderboards over time, weight formula, historical rank-to-selection conversion, injury status and eligibility; for contests, announced participants and past winners' profiles.
nba.all_star_process.mechanism: Fan/player/media voting and league announcements determine starters, reserves, contest entrants and event outcomes.
nba.all_star_process.rationale: All-Star outcomes are driven by published vote tallies (fan, player, media weights), selection rules and injuries/availability; event participation announcements are dated and sourced. Subtle: weights and eligibility rules change by year and the market often resolves on official announcement wording.

free_sources: Official All-NBA voting totals (published after announcement)
nba.allnba_points_ladder.label: All-NBA points ladder and cut-line margins (positionless)
nba.allnba_points_ladder.measurement: Simulate 100 ballots: each voter draws a ranked 15-player list from a Dirichlet-perturbed consensus of candidates' production and team-success scores (concentration alpha=8 per candidate, calibrated to 2023-25 published vote totals); output P(rank<=5), P(rank<=10), P(rank<=15), enforce sums of 5, 10, 15; as-of nightly after the eligibility filter.
nba.allnba_points_ladder.mechanism: All-NBA teams are three five-player cut lines on a single points ranking (5/3/1 for first/second/third team); a candidate's probabilities across team markets are nested.
nba.allnba_points_ladder.rationale: Candidates with similar profiles split votes and a margin of a few points moves a player between teams; ballots are positionless since 2023-24, so the old guard/forward/center constraints no longer bind and should not be modelled.

nba.apology_statement_hazard.label: Public apology hazard after an incident
nba.apology_statement_hazard.measurement: Reference class of NBA incidents with league discipline 2015-2026 coded for apology (public, specific) and days to apology; logistic model on discipline severity (fine, suspension games), injury to the opponent, player's prior apology record, team statement; hazard decays exponentially with a half-life estimated from days-to-apology; as-of: market snapshot, conditioned on days elapsed without an apology.
nba.apology_statement_hazard.mechanism: After an on-court or public incident a player apologises publicly with a probability that rises with league discipline, injury to the other party and media backlash, and that depends on his history.
nba.apology_statement_hazard.rationale: KXNBAAPOLOGY needs a public, topic-specific, non-conditional apology; most apologies occur within days of the incident or the discipline announcement, so the hazard is front-loaded and decays, and players with a pattern of not apologising rarely do so later.

nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.label: All-Star exhibition effort, pace and score variance baseline, conditional on timed vs target format
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.measurement: Split all exhibition games by format vector from nba.contest_format_rules_ledger. Timed games: points per team per minute, 3PA rate, margin SD per 12 minutes and late-compression coefficient (margin SD change over the final 4 minutes). Target games: points per possession for each team and possessions to reach the target, fed to nba.target_score_race_model. Shrink current-format estimates toward the pooled same-regime value (few games per format); as-of = last completed event; units = points and margin SD.
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.mechanism: Exhibition scoring and margin come from low defensive effort, extreme three-point volume and random clustering of makes; how effort evolves depends on whether the game is clock-timed (2026: 12-minute games) or untimed race-to-target (2025 ASG, Rising Stars).
nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline.rationale: Margin variance is large relative to talent gaps, so short games raise the weaker roster's chance. In timed games effort rises in the final minutes and point differential can matter for the tiebreak; in target-score games there is no clock and the end is a race, so the two regimes must not be pooled. The contract year fixes the regime: 2026 KXNBAALLSTARGAME is timed (rules text), KXNBARISINGSTARS is target (rules text).

nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.label: All-Star Game minutes plan, rest and multi-game fatigue
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.measurement: From past games compute minutes per player vs season minutes with an ordinal shrinkage; model P(player plays under 15 minutes) as a function of age, season minutes load and injury report flags; for multi-game formats estimate the drop in minutes for game 2 vs game 1; as-of = injury reports on game day and coach statements; units = minutes per game, probability of reduced role.
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.mechanism: All-Star players play capped minutes with fairly even distribution, and in a multi-game format starters and replacements are managed across games, which changes who is on court in the decisive game.
nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan.rationale: Minutes are not set by merit: coaches are mostly told to share minutes, and players with injuries or heavy loads often log little. In a mini-tournament, a team that must play two games may rotate its stars, while the fresh final-game lineup matters more than the roster list.

free_sources: Basketball-Reference All-Star MVP history and box scores
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.label: All-Star MVP selection model (production on the winning team and voter choice)
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.measurement: Fit on past All-Star MVPs (20+ events): conditional logit over players of the winning team on share of team points, made threes, minutes, starter status, home-market flag and prior All-Star MVP; P(MVP) = sum over teams of P(team champion) from nba.asg_tournament_path_sim x conditional choice, plus a small residual for a non-champion MVP estimated from the historical share of MVPs on losing teams (the champion link is convention, not a rule), with per-player points drawn from usage x minutes plans; multiply by P(participates); as-of = final rosters; units = probability.
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.mechanism: The All-Star MVP is chosen by a selection panel after the event; winners almost always come from the champion team and are the standout scorer or narrative figure, so P(MVP) = P(team wins) x P(selected | team wins, box score, narrative).
nba.asg_mvp_vote_model.rationale: In a tournament with short games the MVP depends on the whole path, and home-market or farewell narratives can beat raw points. The selection method (media panel, any fan component) and whether it covers only the championship game are not in the Kalshi rules, and a withdrawn named player resolves No.

nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.label: All-Star Game team roster strength and composition
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.measurement: For each team sum player ratings weighted by expected minute share from nba.asg_minutes_rotation_plan: rating = w1 x offence impact per 100 (shrunk, placeholder k=500 possessions) + w2 x three-point volume x accuracy + w3 x creation (assist rate); w1-w3 are placeholders (initial 0.5/0.3/0.2) to be fitted on past exhibition margins; apply positional balance adjustment for bigs; output expected margin per 12 minutes for every team pair (three pairs in 2026, six in a four-team format); as-of = final roster after the replacement window.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.mechanism: The Game winner is the team whose assigned players are collectively better at scoring in an open-court, low-defence environment, built from impact, shooting and creation of the players who actually appear.
nba.asg_roster_strength_composite.rationale: Because the same selected stars are split among teams, gaps are small and dominated by composition: shooters and creators gain more than rim protectors in a low-defence game, and replacements change rosters late. In 2026 teams were built by nationality (USA Stars, USA Stripes, World), so one team can be systematically stronger, unlike a draft; in 2025 the drafted teams faced a Rising Stars team of first/second-year players.
raw_data: player offensive impact and three-point volume

free_sources: Format parameters from the rules ledger
Basketball-Reference All-Star box scores for calibration
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.label: All-Star / Rising Stars tournament path simulation (round robin, tiebreaks, final)
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.measurement: Monte Carlo (50000 runs) over the format vector: for timed games draw margin ~ Normal(expected margin from nba.asg_roster_strength_composite x minutes adjustment, SD from nba.asg_effort_scoring_baseline); apply Game-2/Game-3 pairing by Game-1 result, rank by record then point differential (later tiebreak unknown: random, flagged), play the championship; for target formats call nba.target_score_race_model per game; for 2025 sample the Rising Stars entrant from the KXNBARISINGSTARS simulation; output P(champion), P(final) per team; as-of = last roster change.
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.mechanism: Champion probability is the result of a multi-game path: in 2026 three teams play a round robin of 12-minute games where margins feed the point-differential tiebreak, then the top two play a championship; brackets (Rising Stars, 2025 ASG) chain two target-score races.
nba.asg_tournament_path_sim.rationale: A pairwise team gap is not a winner probability: in the 2026 round robin a team's chance depends on its margin distribution in two games (point differential decides a 1-1-1 tie, per rules) and on who it meets in the final; Game 2/3 pairings depend on Game 1's result, so the path is sequential. In 2025 the fourth ASG team was the Rising Stars winner, an entrant unknown until two days before.

nba.assisted_three_passer_map.label: Share of shooter's made threes assisted by each teammate (passer dependence)
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.measurement: From play-by-play assists, compute for each shooter the share of made+missed assisted threes by passer over 2 seasons (shrink shares to team-average share by prior weight 40 attempts); expected change in attempts = sum over passers of share x P(passer out) x (1 - replacement factor), replacement factor estimated from games the passer missed (default 0.65). As-of: injury report vintage.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.mechanism: A catch-and-shoot three requires a passer; the loss of a particular creator removes a specific fraction of assisted looks, with replacement playmakers delivering fewer.
nba.assisted_three_passer_map.rationale: Absence adjustments built from with/without splits ignore that dependence is concentrated in a few passers; in many pairs one creator generates 30-40% of a shooter's threes, so his absence matters far more than other absences.
raw_data: PBP: shooter, assister, made flag, shot type

free_sources: ESPN and The Athletic reporting archives
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.label: Contest field changes: withdrawal and replacement hazard
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.measurement: Per announced entrant: P(withdraw before event) = base rate estimated from past announced fields (placeholder prior 10-15 percent per entrant until counted) updated by current injury status from nba.injuries_pit and by also being in the All-Star Game or Rising Stars; Yes-side probability for a named entrant = P(participates) x P(win | field) because withdrawal resolves No (rules); replacement drawn from next-ranked shooters or dunkers by pedigree; as-of = each daily injury report and announcement.
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.mechanism: The entrant list for the 3-point and dunk contests is announced weeks ahead and changes through injury, rest, ASG replacement and sponsor negotiation, which changes both the field strength and the winner's probability.
nba.asw_field_withdrawal_hazard.rationale: A late replacement is usually weaker or different in type, and a withdrawal of the favourite lifts every remaining entrant; the market question requires a specific named player so this is also an eligibility risk.

nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.label: Season-average state with rounding rule: unrounded to rounded threshold and remaining games
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.measurement: State = (makes to date, games played, games remaining); posterior of the player's rest-of-season average (shrunk) times remaining games plus makes to date gives the final average distribution; compute P(round(final_avg, d) >= strike) = P(final_avg >= strike - 0.5*10^-d) with d = 1 assumed from the strike precision and not confirmed by the rules (the text says only 'rounded figure as reported by the Source Agencies'; verify the decimal places and the half-up rule, sp-source-agencies), include the probability of playing zero games (settles at 0) and the denominator being games actually played. As-of: nightly after games.
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.mechanism: The contract uses the rounded per-game figure from the source agencies, so the effective threshold on the unrounded average is half a rounding unit below the stated strike, and the average itself converges as games accumulate.
nba.avg_rounding_and_games_state.rationale: A 2.6+ three-pointers per game contract resolves on the rounded value, so a true average of 2.55 counts as 2.6 (at one-decimal rounding); ignoring the rounding shifts the threshold and its uncertainty is smaller as the season progresses; zero games played counts as an average of zero.
raw_data: player-game makes, games played, remaining team schedule

nba.award_role_filters.label: Award-specific candidate filters (bench-start ratio, rookie status, clutch minimum)
nba.award_role_filters.measurement: Per award: boolean membership computed from the league definition on as-of date: sixth man requires games_off_bench > games_started; ROY requires rookie flag from the league rookie list; Clutch POY requires clutch minutes (last 5 min, score within 5) >= league minimum; produce candidate list and the gap in the stat the award names (clutch net points, improvement delta in PER/BPM, defensive win shares) with 10-game shrinkage to season value.
nba.award_role_filters.mechanism: Each award has a definitional filter (Sixth Man must come off the bench in more games than he starts, ROY needs rookie status, Clutch POY needs clutch minutes/games, MIP needs improvement versus prior year) that decides who is in the candidate set.
nba.award_role_filters.rationale: A single input called award_stats treats all awards alike, but the candidate set is built by the filter first; a starter promoted mid-season loses Sixth Man eligibility, and a rookie who played overseas may or may not be a rookie.

free_sources: NBA.com award announcements and press releases
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.label: Voting-panel and nominee model for award contracts, including the probability of multiple co-winners
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.measurement: Build an award history table (at least 15 seasons) of nominees or finalists, winner(s) and the number of awardees. Fit a conditional logit for P(winner | nominee) on prior finalist or winner status, team success, and for series MVPs on series points rank and best-player indicator, with ridge regularisation and a prior weight of 10 award-years. Estimate P(more than one awardee) as the historical frequency with a beta(1,10) prior, and the expected payout as P(win) x E[1/N | win] rounded down to the cent. For game-based MVPs multiply by P(team wins the series) from nba.series_model. As-of: before announcement, updated when finalists are published.
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.mechanism: Award contracts such as the Social Justice Champion, Finals MVP, conference finals MVP and Cup All-Tournament selections are decided by a panel or vote among nominees, not by team simulation, so the relevant quantities are the nominee set, the historical winner profile and the chance of several winners.
nba.award_vote_and_cowinner_model.rationale: For KXNBASJC the sampled rules split the payout $1/N among multiple awardees, so P(multiple winners) and the winner's profile (community work and nominee status) matter more than basketball production. For Finals and conference finals MVPs the winner is chosen from the winning team after the series by a panel, so the team simulation only gives the first factor. Panels are small, so narrative and series stats can dominate and the winner is a discrete choice among a few candidates.
raw_data: award winners and number of awardees by year

free_sources: nba_api box score minutes and starters
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.label: Bench minutes distribution (240 + 25k minus starter minutes)
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.measurement: Per team: bench minutes = 240 + 25*OT - Σ starter minutes; model starter minutes as scenario mixture (blowout/close/OT/foul trouble) with weights from own-model margin; bench points = bench minutes × bench points-per-minute with 30-game half-life and shrinkage k=300 minutes; as-of lineups; output mean/sd by scenario.
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.mechanism: Bench points depend on bench minutes first; they equal total team minutes minus starter minutes and shrink when starters play heavy minutes in close games or OT.
nba.bench_minutes_distribution.rationale: The draft's bench input is points share, while the better predictor is minutes times points per minute with a state-dependent minutes distribution.

nba.big_exit_protection_state.label: Big-man early-exit and first-half-only participation hazard, mapped to protected-contract voiding
nba.big_exit_protection_state.measurement: Per player-season, estimate P(minutes in 2H+OT = 0 | entered 1H) and P(exit before 12 total minutes) from play-by-play with beta(2,40) shrinkage and a status multiplier; output separately, by cause (injury or ejection, foul-out, blowout rest of the whole second half): hazard of 'plays only first half' (protected refund branch) and 'exits early without refund'. The blowout-rest cause is estimated as P(no second-half minutes | entered 1H, halftime margin bin) and is driven by nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (rare for starters, common for deep-bench bigs). As-of: injury report vintage.
nba.big_exit_protection_state.mechanism: Protected rebound contracts refund any player who enters in the first half but does not enter after halftime (including overtime), whatever the cause: injury or foul-out, ejection, or a coach resting him for the whole second half of a lopsided game.
nba.big_exit_protection_state.rationale: In standard contracts an early exit settles NO; in protected series the same event refunds at a pre-tip fair price, so the same underlying hazard has opposite market consequences and must be tracked separately for the two forms. Blowout-driven second-half rest is the cause most likely to be missed: a bench big who played 6 first-half minutes in a game that is 25 points at halftime is refunded, so the refund branch also depends on the margin path.

nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.label: Bonus-state and team-foul environment
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.measurement: Opponent team personal fouls per quarter, share of quarter minutes in bonus (from play-by-play), crew fouls per game; combine as bonus_minutes_expected = f(opponent foul rate, crew rate, own pace) using 3 seasons; each bonus minute adds a rate of player-specific non-shooting-foul attempts (estimated from the player's FTA in bonus vs non-bonus minutes with shrinkage k=40 minutes).
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.mechanism: Non-shooting fouls turn into free throws once the defending team is in the bonus, so the opponent's team foul rate and bonus minutes drive attempts.
nba.bonus_state_foul_environment.rationale: Opponent foul rate enters twice (shooting fouls and bonus fouls), and the draft's foul rate input does not separate the bonus effect.
raw_data: foul events with team foul count, quarter, crew

nba.calendar_hazard_profile.label: Calendar hazard profile (deadlines, draft, free agency, board meetings)
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.measurement: Estimate discrete-time hazard by day-of-year landmark offset from 15 seasons of transactions (trades, coach changes, retirements, signings) with kernel smoothing and a landmark dummy set; P(event in remaining window) = 1 - Π(1-h_d) with hazards conditioned on the event not having occurred; incorporate announced meeting dates as known spikes.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.mechanism: Event hazard varies with landmarks: trade deadline, draft week, free-agency opening, league board meetings, season start.
nba.calendar_hazard_profile.rationale: A uniform hazard over the window badly misprices markets with a deadline; most transactions cluster in a few days and the remaining hazard collapses after each landmark.

nba.career_horizon_signals.label: Player career-horizon signals (age, contract years, injury, public statements)
nba.career_horizon_signals.measurement: Per player: age, years remaining on contract, cumulative games missed over last two seasons, minutes trend, explicit retirement statements (coded 0/1/2 by explicitness), compute discrete hazard by age from historical retirements (e.g. age 38+ about 20-25% per year, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) and multiply by an odds factor for explicit statements; effective date constraint from rule wording.
nba.career_horizon_signals.mechanism: Retirement and next-contract markets depend on age, contract expiry, injury burden, role decline and public statements.
nba.career_horizon_signals.rationale: The draft input injury_risk_season is a season games-missed expectation, not a career-horizon hazard; retirement hazard rises with age and with specific signals such as a farewell tour announcement.

nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.label: Margin spread, blowout and starter-truncation profile in close-out and elimination games
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.measurement: From playoff play-by-play 2004+: classify each game by state (clinch opportunity for home/away, elimination for both, neither); fit margin sd, blowout (>=20) probability and starter minutes after a 20-point lead by state, controlling for rating gap and venue, taking the mean elimination shift from nba.series_game_conditional_state; shrink state effects toward the neutral-game values with a prior sd of 2 points on sd-ratio terms.
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.mechanism: When one team can clinch or is facing elimination, effort and rotation decisions change the SPREAD of margins and the blowout and garbage-time profile (a team down 0-3 may concede late; game-7 margins are compressed); the mean shift for elimination games is the dummy in nba.series_game_conditional_state and is not re-estimated here.
nba.clinch_elimination_margin_profile.rationale: The final game of every series is a close-out game, so its margin enters every cumulative differential; if close-out games are more lopsided (or, for game 7s, tighter) than ratings imply, the differential's tails move. Effects are asymmetric by which side is on the brink.
raw_data: playoff play-by-play with score and substitutions

nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.label: Two-player co-appearance probability with rest correlation
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.measurement: Per game, P(both play) = pA pB + rho sqrt(pA(1-pA)pB(1-pB)) with rho estimated from 5 seasons of pair data (team rest days, load management) shrunk to a role prior; over N games P(at least one overlap) = 1 - Π(1 - P_g) with a correction for injury duration (autocorrelation across games); update after each game.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.mechanism: The probability that both players appear in at least one same game (or in many) is a joint availability probability with positive dependence from team rest decisions.
nba.co_appearance_overlap_prob.rationale: Treating two players' availability as independent overstates co-appearance when rest decisions are shared and understates it when injuries are independent.

free_sources: NBA.com tracking time of possession (via nba_api)
nba.co_creator_load.label: Co-creator load (ball-dominant teammates on court)
nba.co_creator_load.measurement: For the player and each teammate compute time of possession and touches per minute over 60 games; co-creator load = sum of the other four players' expected time of possession per minute (from lineup minutes) minus the league-average of the role; regress player's potential assists per minute on load (ridge) with team fixed effects; compute with tonight's expected lineups and scenarios.
nba.co_creator_load.mechanism: The presence of another ball-dominant creator divides initiations and assists.
nba.co_creator_load.rationale: Usage alone cannot distinguish a lone primary creator from a two-creator backcourt; assists fall when the second creator is on the floor and rise when he is out.

free_sources: NBA.com and NBA Communications press releases
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.label: All-Star Weekend format and rules ledger by event and year
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.measurement: Per event-year and per series (3PT, dunk, ASG, Rising Stars, Shooting Stars, MVP): participants, rounds, advancement count, balls per rack, racks, points per ball type (regular, money ball, deep-zone ball), seconds per round, shoot-off rule, dunks per round and attempt limit, judge count and score range, ASG game length or target score, number of teams, team-assignment rule (conference, draft, nationality), round-robin tiebreak order, Rising Stars semifinal/final targets, Shooting Stars team size and scoring, MVP selection method. Each field carries a provenance flag: RULES_TEXT (quoted Kalshi rule, e.g. 70 s, 40/25 targets, 1-1-1 point-differential tiebreak), LEAGUE_RELEASE, or SOURCE_UNVERIFIED; as-of = the league announcement date. Every historical label joins to its own format vector.
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.mechanism: Each event's winner is a deterministic function of the format: racks, balls, money-ball value, time limit, number of rounds, how many advance, tiebreak or shoot-off, dunk attempt caps and judging scale, All-Star Game length, target score and team structure.
nba.contest_format_rules_ledger.rationale: The formats are changed almost every few years (the Game has switched between East-West, captains' draft and a multi-team mini-tournament), so a historical result is only a label for the same process if the format parameters are matched. The subtle part is that a rule change moves variance and ties, not just level: a shorter game or a single-elimination final increases upset probability.

free_sources: NBA Stats shooting splits by closest defender
Past contest box scores on NBA.com
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.label: Transfer of shooter skill to the contest's rack conditions
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.measurement: Per entrant: posterior make rate = precision-weighted mean of (a) catch-and-shoot 3P% on open and wide-open attempts, last 3 seasons, half-life 1 season, shrunk toward league mean with a prior strength k (placeholder 300 attempts, to be fitted by cross-validation on past contests), (b) FT% logit scaled by a fitted slope, (c) past contest make rate shrunk with k (placeholder 75 balls); contest-conditions offset = mean residual of all entrants in the same contest-year (venue-year effect); units = P(make) per ball before location adjustment; as-of = day before.
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.mechanism: Contest make probability is stationary-catch-and-shoot skill from fixed rack spots, with no defender, no movement, rhythm over about a minute and fatigue; it is only partly predicted by game 3P%.
nba.contest_shooting_skill_transfer.rationale: Game 3P% mixes shot difficulty and defence, so contest make rate is better proxied by catch-and-shoot or open-shot 3P%, free-throw skill and past contest make rate, each shrunk because contest samples are 25 balls. Deep-range pull-up shooters can underperform because the contest rewards form repeatability, and a venue's backdrop and rims add a shared level shift.
raw_data: catch-and-shoot attempts and makes by defender distance

free_sources: nba_api team box scores (reb, oreb, dreb, team reb)
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.label: Player-creditable rebound pool: misses net of team rebounds and dead-ball leakage
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.measurement: For each team-game: creditable_pool = FG misses + live FT misses (last free throw of a trip) - (team rebounds + out-of-bounds recoveries); estimate team-level leakage ratio by regressing team rebounds on FG misses, FT trips and out-of-bounds counts over 2 seasons with 80-game half-life; project tonight's pool as projected combined misses (ratings and shot-quality based, not market totals) times (1 - projected leakage). Leakage uses opponent foul rate and arena (scorer) effect.
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.mechanism: Official player rebounds exclude team rebounds (shot-clock violations, balls out of bounds, first free-throw misses of a pair), so the pool a player can be credited from is smaller than total misses and varies by game flow.
nba.creditable_rebound_pool.rationale: A pool built from field-goal misses alone overstates supply when games have many foul-heavy trips, where missed first free throws and dead-ball team rebounds produce no player rebound; the leakage share is hypothesised to be of the order of 6-10% of misses (unverified, to be estimated from team rebound counts; see pr-leakage-source) and should vary with foul rate.
raw_data: team box scores incl. team rebound counts

nba.cross_league_title_combo.label: Cross-league championship pair probability (NBA title x NHL Stanley Cup) with early-elimination path
nba.cross_league_title_combo.measurement: P_NBA from the NBA title simulation (nba.title_path over simulated seeds, at least 10,000 bracket draws, as-of the quote timestamp); P_NHL from the NHL catalog's championship model at the same timestamp; joint = P_NBA x P_NHL, with independence checked on historical seasons (correlation of title indicators for same-metro NBA/NHL pairs, expected near zero). Also output P(both alive after each playoff round) by combining the two round-survival curves, and set the value to zero at either elimination.
nba.cross_league_title_combo.mechanism: P(Yes) = P(named NBA team wins the title) x P(named NHL team wins the Stanley Cup), with no shared games or players to create dependence; Yes is lost at the first elimination of either team.
nba.cross_league_title_combo.rationale: KXNBANHL is the only live series under this key and it is a futures pair, not a same-game parlay, so none of the same-game dependence inputs apply. The NHL probability is outside the NBA catalog and must come from the NHL model on the same as-of timestamp; the subtle parts are the path (elimination of either leg ends the contract early) and that thin, longshot-heavy pair prices are where market miscalibration is likely, which this input must not borrow from prices.
raw_data: NBA title simulation output by team and round
NHL title simulation output by team and round (from the NHL model)
playoff elimination dates in both leagues

nba.cross_player_points_dependence.label: Dependence of points across players (teammates, opponents, same player multi-stat)
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.measurement: Estimate pairwise correlations of residual points (actual minus minutes-conditional expectation) for same-team and opposite-team pairs over a 2-season window with Fisher-z shrinkage toward position-pair prior (weight 40 games); also correlation of a player's points with his own rebounds+assists residuals for PRA/PR/PA products. Cross-team pairs typically near +0.1 via pace; same-team pairs typically negative.
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.mechanism: Teammates compete for the same possessions (negative within team conditional on total) while all players share pace and shooting variance of the game (positive across teams), which sets joint-event probabilities.
nba.cross_player_points_dependence.rationale: Head-to-head, combined-stat and points-leader products are functions of the joint law of several players' points; marginals alone give wrong answers, e.g. two opponent stars' point difference has a variance depending on the sign of their correlation.
raw_data: player-game residuals from the minutes-conditional model

nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.label: Probability of a specific Cup Finals pairing as the product of two conference bracket outcomes
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.measurement: Compute P(team A reaches final) from group-stage results (qualifier probability), quarterfinal bracket draw and single-game win probabilities (neutral-site, with rest) and similarly for team B in the other bracket; P(pair) = P(A reaches final) x P(B reaches final) under independence across conference brackets (verify bracket structure from rules). As-of: nightly during the Cup. Independence across the two brackets is an approximation: if both semifinals are played at one neutral site on a shared schedule (unverified), common rest, travel and injury shocks add positive correlation, so also compute P(pair) under a copula with a correlation parameter fitted or bounded, and report the range.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.mechanism: The Cup Finals pair is formed by the two semifinal winners (one from each conference bracket, if the bracket is conference-based), so the pair probability is a product of two independent single-elimination outcomes.
nba.cup_finals_pair_probability.rationale: The matchup contract resolves immediately upon qualification, not when the game is played; its probability depends on group results, quarterfinal and semifinal match-ups and neutral-site single-game probabilities.

nba.cup_format.label: NBA Cup group/knockout structure and tiebreakers
nba.cup_format.measurement: Enumerate remaining group games with margin/tiebreaker simulation, apply wildcard rules, knockout bracket at neutral site; adjust for star minutes and motivation.
nba.cup_format.mechanism: Cup outcomes depend on group-stage point-differential tiebreakers, wildcard rules and single-elimination knockout games, with unusual incentives and neutral sites.
nba.cup_format.rationale: Group-stage point differential makes blowout margins matter in Cup games; rest decisions and star availability vary relative to regular-season games; the knockout games are neutral-site single games. Subtle: rules details change by season and the settlement rule for Cup counts must be read from official documentation.
raw_data: NBA Cup group and knockout results

nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.label: Cup group standings state with point-differential tiebreak and remaining-games simulation
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.measurement: From the Cup schedule compute standings, point differential and head-to-head results to date; simulate the remaining group games with margin distributions from team ratings (sd about 13 points per game) and apply the official group tiebreak order and wildcard rule to produce P(group winner), P(qualifier by wildcard); update after each Cup game. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.mechanism: Cup group qualifiers are decided by group record then tiebreakers (head-to-head, point differential and so on), so the state is a table with a margin component that rewards running up scores in some games.
nba.cup_group_tiebreak_state.rationale: Group-winner and qualifier contracts depend on remaining games, but also on margin of victory in each game because the point-differential tiebreak influences outcomes; a win/loss-only simulation misses this.
raw_data: Cup schedule, results with margins, tiebreak order

nba.dd_category_pair_mix.label: Category-pair decomposition of a player's double-double paths (pts/reb/ast/stl/blk)
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.measurement: For each player-game with >=12 minutes over current + prior 2 seasons, flag each of 5 categories >=10; compute per-category P(>=10 | minutes bucket 12-20/20-28/28-34/34+) with exponential half-life of 45 games and beta shrinkage toward the position-archetype mean with prior weight 20 games; build pair-path rates P(pair) via joint empirical counts (not products). Output per player: vector of pair-path rates and the share of historical DDs coming from each pair. As-of: only games finished before the tip-off timestamp.
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.mechanism: A DD is a union over category pairs; each pair has its own minutes-sensitivity, so the player's probability is a mixture of path-specific probabilities.
nba.dd_category_pair_mix.rationale: A center reaches DD mainly via points+rebounds, a point-forward via points+assists, a rim-protecting big via reb+blk; one scalar 'DD rate' averages over paths whose responses to minutes, blowouts and absences differ, and omits the blocks/steals paths that the contract explicitly counts.

nba.dd_center_swap_share.label: Rebound/assist share conditional on which co-big or creator shares the floor
nba.dd_center_swap_share.measurement: From stint-level data compute the player's TRB% and AST% per lineup context (with each frequent teammate on/off, min 150 possessions) using ridge-regularised on/off coefficients (lambda tuned by rolling CV on prior season); then project tonight's expected minute-weighted lineup mix from rotation history and injury report and sum. Report a minutes-weighted expected board share and assist share with their standard errors.
nba.dd_center_swap_share.mechanism: Boards and assist chances are split among on-court teammates, so a player's DD path depends on which specific teammates occupy the other four slots in each rotation segment.
nba.dd_center_swap_share.rationale: Season rebound or assist percentage averages over very different lineups; the relevant quantity is the player's share when paired with tonight's expected 5-man units, weighted by expected minutes in each unit.

free_sources: nba_api hustle stats (leaguehustlestatsplayer, game-level boxscorehustlev2; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for per-game availability)
nba.deflection_rate.label: Deflections and steal-conversion rate per 36 minutes (hustle stats)
nba.deflection_rate.measurement: Compute deflections per 36 minutes and steals per deflection from hustle-stat tracking for the last 2 seasons with 45-game half-life; shrink conversion to league mean (about 0.20 steals per deflection) with prior weight 80 deflections; expected steals per minute = deflection rate x shrunk conversion; adjust for opponent live-ball turnover propensity. As-of: games before tip.
nba.deflection_rate.mechanism: A steal is a conversion of a deflection or a pass interception; deflections are a more stable measure of defensive activity than steals and predict future steals better than past steals do.
nba.deflection_rate.rationale: Steal counts are 0-3 per game with huge sampling noise; a player's deflection rate and his conversion rate (steals per deflection) separate persistent skill from luck and respond to scheme (gamble-heavy teams generate more of both).
raw_data: hustle: deflections, steals, minutes per game

nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.label: Draft lottery combinatorial odds by pre-lottery rank, including ties and the four-pick rule
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.measurement: Encode the current lottery's 1,000 (or 14 x ...) combination allocation by rank 1-14, compute exact P(pick k | rank r) for k=1..14 (including the rule that teams cannot fall more than 4 positions and ties in record are broken by random drawing before the lottery); combine with the simulated distribution of final regular-season ranks from the standings simulation (include play-in losers) to get P(top-3 pick | team). As-of: nightly; rules versioned by draft year.
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.mechanism: Pick position for non-playoff teams is a random draw with fixed odds by rank (worst three teams each 14.0% for the top pick, no team falling more than four slots, under the current lottery rules (to be re-confirmed for the draft year)), so draft-position contracts reduce to rank odds times a rank distribution.
nba.draft_lottery_odds_table.rationale: Draft top-3/top-5/top-10 contracts are decided by the lottery, which is a known combinatorial mechanism; the uncertainty is the pre-lottery rank (final record, ties, coin flips) and the team's pick ownership, not the draw itself.
raw_data: published lottery combination table by draft year
final regular-season standings with tiebreak draws

free_sources: public mock drafts and big boards (ESPN, The Athletic summaries, Tankathon)
nba.draft_order_joint_simulation.label: Joint draft-order simulation with prospect attributes
nba.draft_order_joint_simulation.measurement: Plackett-Luce (or rank-ordered logit) over prospects with worth parameters from the median of 5+ public big boards (log-worth from consensus rank, dispersion from board sd, shrink k=3 boards), plus team-need adjustments for owners of slots 1-14 from roster position gaps; simulate 20,000 drafts with slot ownership from nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph; attach prospect attributes (college class year, conference, international flag) from roster databases; compute each market's functional per draw; as-of: board snapshot timestamp, updated daily in the final two weeks and hourly on draft day.
nba.draft_order_joint_simulation.mechanism: The full draft order is one random permutation shaped by team-slot ownership, consensus board ranks, board dispersion and team need; every draft market is a functional of that permutation.
nba.draft_order_joint_simulation.rationale: Range, matchup, count and comparison markets (top-N, first 33, A before B, freshmen in the top 10, ACC count equal to Big 12) cannot be priced coherently from per-slot marginals: they depend on the joint ordering and on prospect attributes, and the equality and 'at least 9 of 10' events sit in the tails of sums of correlated indicators.
raw_data: prospect class year, college conference, nationality

nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.label: Draft pick ownership graph with protections and swaps
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.measurement: Table per pick: original team, current owner, protection (top-N range), swap counterpart and conveyance date; for each lottery outcome, determine slot and holder using the protection rules; as-of timestamp = latest completed trade; join with simulated standings to yield P(owner holds slot k).
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.mechanism: Which franchise holds slot N depends on lottery results filtered through traded-pick protections, swap rights and conveyance order across years.
nba.draft_pick_ownership_graph.rationale: Team-to-draft and slot markets require knowing owner(s) and conditions; an unconditional top-4 protected pick converts to a future obligation and changes incentives of both teams in the standings race.

nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.label: Dunk difficulty tier and make probability under attempt caps
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.measurement: Classify each past dunk by difficulty tier (360 or windmill, leap over a person, double-ball, two-step, prop-assisted) from video-coded tags; compute per-dunker attempt success by tier with Beta(2,2) shrinkage, and expected score per dunk = P(make before cap) times mean judged score of the tier plus (1 - P) times the miss score; as-of = last contest participated; units = points per dunk.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.mechanism: A contestant's score depends on choosing a dunk of a given difficulty tier and converting it within the attempt allowance; misses burn time or attempts and zero or lower the score.
nba.dunk_difficulty_make_model.rationale: Hard dunks have a high ceiling but a real miss rate, and the attempt cap makes the score a mixture between a clean mid-tier dunk and a failed high-tier one. Props, teammate assists and limited rehearsal affect conversion; contestants who tend to over-script get penalised for misses.

free_sources: NBA.com contest recaps with judge scores
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.label: Dunk Contest judging panel score and tiebreak model
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.measurement: From past contests extract every dunk's judge scores; fit an ordinal model of dunk score on (attempt number, make flag, prop use, dunker's reputation, round, panel mean leniency) with a partial-pooling judge effect; estimate per-panel mean and SD and the probability of a perfect score; store panel composition as announced (as-of = announcement); output expected round-one totals, P(advance), final-round two-dunk totals (round one does not carry over) and P(tie) per finalist pair. Use only rounds since the current scale was introduced.
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.mechanism: The winner is selected by a panel's subjective scores per dunk; round-one two-dunk totals pick the two finalists and the finalists' two final-round dunks alone decide the champion (rules); panel composition, scoring scale and the compression of scores near the maximum decide who wins and whether a dunk-off is needed.
nba.dunk_judge_score_model.rationale: Scores cluster at the top of the scale so many dunks tie, and a run of 10s from celebrity judges can erase a difficulty advantage. Judges anchor on crowd reaction and narrative as well as difficulty, creating a first-mover and last-mover effect, and repeat winners can be penalised or rewarded depending on the panel's era.

free_sources: NBA Draft Combine measurements (drafted players only)
Basketball-Reference and G League play-by-play dunk counts
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.label: Dunker athletic profile and prior contest record
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.measurement: Per entrant: prior contest finishes (win=3, final=2, appeared=1) with decay 0.7 per year (placeholder), combine max vertical z-score among entrants where measured (missing for undrafted entrants: impute field mean plus a missing flag), in-game dunk count per 100 minutes over the last two seasons combining NBA and G League play-by-play, shrunk with k=200 minutes (placeholder), and a G League/non-NBA flag; combine as a rank-based composite within the announced field; as-of = field announcement date.
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.mechanism: Contest strength comes from leaping ability, creativity and show experience, none of which appear in regular-season box scores.
nba.dunker_pedigree_profile.rationale: Contest entrants are often bench or G League players whose NBA stats say little, so talent is measured by prior contest finishes, highlight dunk rate, vertical measures from draft combine and age. The sample is tiny and selection is heavy, so pedigree must be shrunk toward a field mean and treated as a ranking, not a number.

nba.early_exit_hazard.label: Protected-void probability: first-half-only participation (injury, ejection, illness or coach-rested second half)
nba.early_exit_hazard.measurement: Two components over the last 3 seasons. (a) Injury/ejection/illness exit hazard h = exits (left and did not return) / minutes, shrunk to a position prior with k=2000 minutes and scaled by 1.5 for the first 3 games after a listed injury; P(exit before half) = 1 - exp(-h*minutes_in_half1). (b) Coach-rest route: from play-by-play, P(no second-half entry | played first half and non-injury) by own-model pregame spread bucket and coach, estimated on 3 seasons with beta shrinkage k=30 games; combine as 1-(1-a)(1-b); then convert by contract wording (protected void vs actual stats, with the strike-already-reached carve-out).
nba.early_exit_hazard.mechanism: P(player enters in the first half but never after halftime, including OT) = injury/ejection/illness exit hazard plus the coach decision to rest him for the whole second half in a lopsided game; the protected clause voids both unless the strike was already reached.
nba.early_exit_hazard.rationale: Early exit by injury is only one route to the void state: the sampled protected text voids any player who enters in the first half and does not enter after it, so a starter pulled for the entire second half of a first-half blowout is also void. Both routes are unrelated to per-minute rates and the second is strongly tied to the first-half margin.

nba.early_game_usage_first6.label: Early-game usage (first six minutes) by starter
nba.early_game_usage_first6.measurement: Per starter: FGA+0.44*FTA share and made-FG share within the first 6 minutes of Q1 across last 60 games (half-life 25), shrunk toward the player's overall usage with k=120 early-game team attempts; renormalise across tonight's expected starters; combine with first_basket_share by precision weighting.
nba.early_game_usage_first6.mechanism: The share of team shot attempts and made baskets taken by each starter in the first six minutes of the game, where scripted plays and starter minutes dominate.
nba.early_game_usage_first6.rationale: First-basket history is a handful of events per player; the first six minutes of play produce far more observations (about 12-18 attempts per team per game) and reflect the script.
raw_data: play-by-play with period clock and shooter

nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.label: Qualifying-games ledger (65 games with 20+ minutes) and slack
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.measurement: Per player: qualifying = games with minutes >= 20 (allow up to 2 games of 15-20 minutes per league rule, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the 2026-27 rule); slack = games_remaining - (65 - qualifying); P(eligible) = P(missed games among remaining <= slack) under a Poisson-binomial with per-game miss probability = player-season availability rate shrunk with k=20 games toward position prior, updated nightly after the 6pm ET injury report; as-of timestamp = last completed game. Apply the ledger only to awards the league criteria say it governs (flag per award; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED), and not to monthly awards, Coach or Executive of the Year, All-Star selection or draft markets.
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.mechanism: The award eligibility count is a deterministic ledger that only the league's definition of a qualifying game updates; slack to the line plus injury hazard gives the probability of staying eligible.
nba.eligibility_minutes_ledger.rationale: The existing eligibility input restates the rule but not the arithmetic; a player at 50 qualifying games with 20 left has a very different conditional risk from one at 62 with a nagging injury, and games of 15-20 minutes count only in a small allowance.

nba.expectation_overperformance.label: Wins minus preseason expectation (own, non-market)
nba.expectation_overperformance.measurement: exp_wins_pre = 82 x (own preseason team rating converted via Pythagorean with exponent 14, using returning minutes-weighted player ratings with 0.6 weight on last season, 0.4 on career, regressed 30% to league mean); surprise = wins_to_date - exp_wins_pre scaled by sd 6 wins; recompute on the as-of date using games played to date + 82 - GP times current rating.
nba.expectation_overperformance.mechanism: Coach, Executive, MIP and team-driven awards reward results above what the roster implied before the season, so voters compare wins to a preseason baseline.
nba.expectation_overperformance.rationale: Total wins alone ranks the best teams first, but Coach of the Year goes to the largest positive surprise; the baseline must be an own rating-based preseason projection and not a sportsbook win total to avoid a market-derived input.

nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.label: Field-goal attempts per minute split into two-point and three-point attempts, with free-throw trip rate
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.measurement: 2PA, 3PA and FTA per 36 minutes over the last 2 seasons with weights 0.6 recent / 0.4 prior and half-life 20 games, shrunk to the role-position mean with k=300 minutes; scale by the projected minutes scenario mixture and add the with/without-teammate shift from the teammate-absence splits; output a per-minute rate and its sd for use in a negative-binomial attempt model.
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.mechanism: Points = 2 x made 2PT + 3 x made 3PT + FTM, so each component needs its own attempt rate per minute rather than a blended usage rate that includes turnovers.
nba.fga_per_minute_by_shot_type.rationale: The points escalator needs FGA per minute by type and free-throw trips per minute as the volume base for the cubic payout; usage rate mixes in turnovers and free-throw trips, and the audit of nba.usage asks for this replacement.

nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.label: Empirical final-margin pmf by own-model mean and sd
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.measurement: Collect 15 seasons of final signed margins; standardise z = (margin - mu_own)/sigma_own using own-model mean and sd; estimate the pmf of the integer margin by kernel smoothing of the z-density plus an explicit multiplicative correction per integer margin in [-12, 12] (ridge-shrunk to 1); validate by log-loss of band probabilities in 2 held-out seasons; recompute annually.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.mechanism: The final margin has non-smooth pmf structure (hole at zero, OT bump, late-game parity) that a normal density does not reproduce.
nba.final_margin_pmf_empirical.rationale: The draft names score_resid as the margin density by spread bucket, but spread buckets from market lines are circular and the pmf structure lives at the integer level; band edges at 5/6 and 10/11 fall exactly on such structure.

nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.label: Probability a given player wins Finals/Conference Finals MVP conditional on his team winning the series
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.measurement: From 20 seasons of Finals and Conference Finals results compute for each champion's top-3 players the share of MVP awards by rank in series points, by pre-series team star ranking and by minutes share; fit a conditional logit on pre-series expected points rank and best-player indicator (pre-series BPM rank), regularised; output P(MVP | team wins) by player. Combine with series win probability from the series model. As-of: before series start (updated per game).
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.mechanism: Award contracts are conditional on the team winning and then on voter choice among its players, which follows stat shares and narrative in the series.
nba.finals_mvp_given_title_share.rationale: Finals MVP of a champion usually goes to the top scorer or best player of the series, with media voters weighing series scoring, efficiency and team role; P(player MVP) = P(team wins) x P(player chosen | team wins) and the second factor can be estimated from past award results.
raw_data: Finals and conference-finals MVP winners with series box scores

nba.first_passage_race_table.label: Empirical race-to-N first-passage table by N, opening possession and early-game rating gap
nba.first_passage_race_table.measurement: From 5 seasons of play-by-play compute for each game and each N in {5,10,15,20,25,30} which team reached N first, whether that team had the opening possession and the starters' first-stint net rating gap; fit logistic regressions per N with covariates (opening possession, rating gap, home) and ridge shrinkage; output P(win race) with standard errors. Rating gap uses the first-stint rating below, not full-game rating.
nba.first_passage_race_table.mechanism: First-to-N is a first-passage problem on two alternating-possession scoring processes with lumpy increments; the answer depends on N, who has the ball first and the early-game scoring rate gap.
nba.first_passage_race_table.rationale: Treating the race as two independent Poisson clocks mispredicts because possessions alternate and scores come in 1-3 point lumps; the first-possession advantage is hypothesised to be about half a possession (unverified) and its relative value shrinks with N, so a table by N is needed. Scope: single-game race-to-N only; it does not describe a season-long first-to-threshold contract.
raw_data: PBP scoring events with clock and team running totals

nba.first_possession_chain_prob.label: Opening-possession race probability (team scores first)
nba.first_possession_chain_prob.measurement: pA = team A opening-possession scoring proxy under the contract definition: share of games in which A's first trip produced a made FG (if free throws do not count) or at least one made shot or free throw (if they do), computed over last 2 seasons with 15-game half-life and shrunk to league 0.50 with k=40 games; pB similar for B; P(A first) = P(A wins tip) * pA/(1-(1-pA)(1-pB)) + (1-P(A wins tip)) * [1 - pB/(1-(1-pA)(1-pB))]; P(A wins tip) = 0.5 + 0.1*(jumper tip rate - 0.5) with the two starting jumpers' last-two-season tip win rates shrunk with k=15 tips.
nba.first_possession_chain_prob.mechanism: Probability that team A scores first given tip result and each team's opening-possession conversion rate: pA/(1-(1-pA)(1-pB)).
nba.first_possession_chain_prob.rationale: The existing tip input treats tip win as the driver, but the tip only fixes who starts the race; the conversion rates on both sides decide it and the formula shows why the tip's effect is only a few points. At pA = pB = 0.5 the race formula gives 0.667 for the team holding the ball, so a tip win is worth about 2-3 points of team-first probability, not more.

nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.label: First-attempt shot-type mix and make probability
nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.measurement: From the first FGA of each team-game for 3 seasons, tabulate type (rim, corner 3, above-break 3, mid) per player; make probability = type-specific league rate (rim .62, corner 3 .38, ATB 3 .36, mid .42, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) shrunk to the player's type-specific rate with k=50 attempts; weight by tonight's opponent allowed rate in that zone for the first 6 minutes.
nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.mechanism: The opening shot is more likely a rim attempt or a catch-and-shoot three off a set play, and the make rate depends on that type.
nba.first_shot_type_make_prob.rationale: The existing shot_profile is season-wide but the opening plays use their own distribution; a player whose first shots are layups has a higher conversion than the same player's season average.

nba.four_factors_matchup.label: Expected four factors for own offense vs opponent defense (eFG%, turnover rate, offensive rebound rate, free-throw rate)
nba.four_factors_matchup.measurement: For each team compute offensive and defensive four factors per 100 possessions over last 25 games (half-life 12) and season, opponent-adjusted by the standard iterative method; expected eFG = league + (own offense - league) + (opp defense allowed - league) with team-specific shrinkage weights (prior weight 20 games); combine factors into expected points per 100 using regression weights (eFG about 0.4, TOV 0.25, ORB 0.2, FT 0.15). As-of: games before tip, with lineup adjustments for absentees.
nba.four_factors_matchup.mechanism: Team points per possession decompose into shooting efficiency, turnovers, offensive rebounds and free-throw rate; each factor responds to the specific opponent differently than the overall rating does.
nba.four_factors_matchup.rationale: Offensive rating against defensive rating is an additive approximation; a rim-heavy offense against a drop defense, or a turnover-prone offense against a pressure defense, deviates from it, and the factor-level decomposition allows shot profile, scheme and luck to enter in the right place.
raw_data: team game box scores: FGM, FG3M, FGA, TOV, OREB, FTA, possessions

nba.ft_skill_posterior.label: Free-throw skill posterior (career, three-point, pre-NBA priors)
nba.ft_skill_posterior.measurement: p_hat = (FTM_3y_weighted + a) / (FTA_3y_weighted + a + b), with weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 by season, prior (a, b) from a regression of FT% on 3P% (slope about 0.5 at 100 3PA, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED) and pre-NBA FT% for rookies, effective prior size 80 attempts; report sd of posterior.
nba.ft_skill_posterior.mechanism: Make probability is a skill with informative priors for low-sample players.
nba.ft_skill_posterior.rationale: Free-throw percentage over a short sample is noisy; for rookies and low-volume players, three-point percentage and pre-NBA free-throw data improve the estimate.
raw_data: career FT and 3P attempts and makes

nba.ft_trip_structure_model.label: Free-throw trip generation model (trips x attempts per trip)
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.measurement: Per player: trips per 36 = shooting-foul trips (per 100 rim attempts and per 100 post touches) + bonus trips (per team-bonus minute) + other; attempts per trip distribution from his shot mix (share of 3PA fouled, and-one rate); estimate with 3 seasons of play-by-play, shrinkage k=60 trips to position prior; simulate trips with negative-binomial dispersion estimated across games.
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.mechanism: Attempts are the sum of trips (shooting fouls, bonus fouls, technicals, intentional fouls) times attempts per trip (1, 2, 3).
nba.ft_trip_structure_model.rationale: The draft's ft_attempts is a rate; the clustered structure of trips matters for the variance and for the survival function at N.

nba.game_factor_loadings.label: Game-level latent factor loadings by leg type
nba.game_factor_loadings.measurement: Fit a Gaussian-copula factor model on 6 seasons of game-level outcomes: observed leg indicators (spread covers, total overs, player N+ at typical thresholds) transformed to normal scores via marginal CDFs; estimate loadings with 3 factors (total, margin, team luck) per team-side and role cell (starter guard, wing, big) with ridge shrinkage; report loadings and sd across 100 bootstrap draws; as-of end of the previous game.
nba.game_factor_loadings.mechanism: Legs load on shared factors (pace/total, margin, team shooting luck, availability) with loadings that differ by leg type and player role.
nba.game_factor_loadings.rationale: The draft lists covariance of a single player's stats, but multi-leg dependence spans legs from different mechanisms; a factor model captures it with a manageable parameter count.

nba.game_pace_composition.label: Game-pace composition rule from two teams' tempos
nba.game_pace_composition.measurement: Regress game possessions on (paceA + paceB)/2, |paceA - paceB|, each team's transition-frequency and turnover rate and rest, using 5 seasons of team-games with opponent-adjusted paces (20-game half-life); report coefficients and residual sd; as-of the last completed game; adjust for active set via nba.absence_pace_efficiency_decomposition.
nba.game_pace_composition.mechanism: Expected game possessions as a function of both teams' pace, transition frequency and turnover rates rather than a simple average.
nba.game_pace_composition.rationale: The draft states that the slower team controls tempo; the empirical rule must be fitted, with transition frequency and defence-forced turnovers as additional terms.

nba.governance_approval_pipeline.label: Deal-stage ledger and league approval pipeline
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.measurement: For each live deal record stage, date entered, and the historical distribution of days to the next stage from past NBA and other major-league sales (log-normal fit per stage, shrunk to cross-league pooled values with k=3 deals); compute P(reach required stage by T) = Π P(transition) × P(duration sum <= T-t); update when a stage is entered; attach the league approval vote threshold as a feasibility gate (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for the exact threshold).
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.mechanism: Sales, relocations and expansions pass through stages (exploration, exclusivity, definitive agreement, governance vote, closing) with stage-specific completion odds and delays.
nba.governance_approval_pipeline.rationale: A rumor-level input cannot tell whether a deal is two weeks or five months from the qualifying stage, and the contracts require specific stages; the pipeline gives P(complete by date).

nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.label: Probability of heavy-minutes games (38+ minutes, OT)
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.measurement: Per player: share of games with minutes >= 38 over the last 80 games (half-life 30), shrunk to role prior with k=15 games; condition on own-model closeness (P(|margin| < 8) from the margin model) and OT probability 0.06; produce P(minutes >= 38) and mean count in that regime = rate per minute x 40; as-of lineup status.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.mechanism: The extreme counts come from nights with heavy minutes, whose probability depends on game closeness, depth and the coach's usage of the star.
nba.heavy_minutes_tail_prob.rationale: A single projected minutes figure hides the 10-20% of nights with 38+ minutes that produce the top bands, and nights with 20-25 minutes that produce the bottom ones.

nba.hof_committee_vote_model.label: Hall of Fame election model: finalist stage, honors-committee vote and direct-elect paths
nba.hof_committee_vote_model.measurement: From the Hall's published finalist lists and inductee classes for at least 15 years, fit two logistic models by category (NBA player, coach, contributor, international, women): P(finalist | eligible) and P(inducted | finalist), on career markers (players: All-NBA selections, titles, All-Star count, career Win Shares; coaches: regular-season wins, playoff series won, titles, seasons as head coach) and years since eligibility, ridge-penalised with a prior weight of 5 classes; direct-elect committee picks are a separate category frequency. As-of: the market timestamp; switch to P(inducted | finalist) once finalists are announced. The vote threshold (recalled as 18 of 24) is unverified (u8).
nba.hof_committee_vote_model.mechanism: A candidate is inducted only after reaching the finalist list and then clearing the honors committee's supermajority, or through a direct-elect committee, so P(inductee) = P(finalist) x P(elected | finalist) or the direct-elect probability.
nba.hof_committee_vote_model.rationale: KXNBAHALLOFFAME settles on being announced as an inductee of the 2027 class and resolves No if the class is announced without the person, so the target is a committee election and not an on-court quantity. Class size is not fixed, so candidates do not strictly crowd each other out; the finalist announcement is the largest information jump; coaches, contributors and international players follow different committees and bars, and a candidate's years on the ballot shift the odds.

nba.implied_team_totals.label: Market-implied team points from spread and total
nba.implied_team_totals.measurement: implied_home = (T - S)/2 and implied_away = (T + S)/2 where S is home spread (negative = home favorite); deviation from the team's season average points; movement since open.
nba.implied_team_totals.mechanism: Spread and total jointly imply each team's expected points, which translate into possessions and efficiency for every player in that game.
nba.implied_team_totals.rationale: Team implied total = (total ± spread)/2. Player props (points, assists, rebounds, threes) scale with team points and with the game's pace, and the implied totals move on injury news before box-score features update. It is the compact summary of the book's view of pace and offense in this exact matchup with current availability.

nba.injuries_pit.label: Injury report (official + ESPN) vintages, status changes

nba.injuries_pit.mechanism: Player status (out, doubtful, questionable, probable) as of a timestamp determines who plays, and hence minutes, usage and team strength.
nba.injuries_pit.rationale: The official report is posted in waves (afternoon the day before, updates through game day) and final inactives appear ~30-90 minutes before tip, so at a given decision time status is often only partially resolved. nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.label: Intentional-foul target probability (hack-a policy and late-game ball handlers)
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.measurement: Per player: attempts in the last 2 minutes of games within 6 points per 100 such minutes (last 3 seasons, shrinkage k=30 minutes); logistic target model with features FT% (below 0.60 flag), ball-handler role, trailing/leading, margin; combine with own-model P(close at 2:00) to give expected additional attempts; update each season after rule changes. Add an early-game component: frequency of intentional away-from-the-ball or hack-a fouls in Q1-Q3 per 100 possessions by opposing coach and target (from play-by-play foul descriptions); outside the last two minutes these are ordinary personal fouls that yield free throws only through the bonus, so they are modelled as extra bonus-state attempts for the targeted low-FT% player.
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.mechanism: Probability that the player is fouled intentionally in the last two minutes of a close game, as a function of FT%, role and margin. Mid-game hack-a-player fouling in Q1-Q3 is included as a separate, rarer component.
nba.intentional_foul_target_prob.rationale: Late-game attempts form the right tail; whether a player is a target depends on a threshold in FT% for bigs and on being the leading team's ball handler.

nba.joint_pace_interaction.label: Joint matchup pace from both teams' pace preferences (slower-team weight and transition vs half-court)
nba.joint_pace_interaction.measurement: From 5 seasons of games regress game possessions on both teams' season paces (adjusted for home), their interaction and style flags (transition share, post-up share) to get weights (the weight on the slower team is a free parameter to be estimated; 0.55 is only an illustrative value, not a finding); add lineup adjustment from projected starters; residual sd by matchup type (fast-fast, fast-slow). Output expected possessions and sd. As-of: tip.
nba.joint_pace_interaction.mechanism: Game possessions are one shared number whose expectation is not the average of two teams' paces; a hypothesis to test is that the slower style dominates and transition-heavy teams are constrained by opponent turnovers and rebounds.
nba.joint_pace_interaction.rationale: A team's total depends on the shared possession count, so error in the pace of the matchup translates directly into points; averaging season paces misstates a matchup of a fast team vs a slow team.

nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.label: Coach-level tie-forcing and intentional-foul policy
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.measurement: From play-by-play: in games within 3 points with <30 seconds left, share of trailing-team possessions ending in a 3PA, a 2PA or a foul-drawn FT; leading-team foul-up-3 rate; compute per coach over 3 seasons (min 15 events) with shrinkage k=10 events to league mean; produce per-matchup tie-conditional probability = P(close at 30s) × P(tie | close, policies).
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.mechanism: How often a team trailing by 2-3 in the last 30 seconds attempts a tying three or a fast two, and how often the leading team fouls up three.
nba.last_possession_tie_attempt_rate.rationale: Excess tie mass comes from end-of-game choices; teams differ, and the same game state yields a tie more often when the trailing coach shoots for the tie than when he fouls and hopes.

nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.label: Late-game stat-chase and teammate-gifting effect near the 10 threshold
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.measurement: From play-by-play, take all instances where a player enters the final 8 game minutes with margin >=12 and a category count of 8 or 9; compute observed rate of reaching 10 per remaining on-court minute divided by that player's baseline per-minute rate in the same category; pool by coach with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (prior weight 25 instances) and report the multiplier. Use as a pregame-fixed multiplier applied only inside the blowout branch.
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.mechanism: When a player sits at 9 rebounds or assists in a decided game, teammates and coaches have been observed to funnel the last opportunity, so production near the threshold is not a smooth Poisson continuation.
nba.late_threshold_assist_rebound_giftin.rationale: Garbage-time minutes are normally a pure loss for DD, but stat-chasing partially offsets it; the size is team and coach specific and can be estimated from play-by-play without any market data. It is subtle because it only applies at 8-9 counts with margin >12 late.
raw_data: PBP event stream with score margin and player counts

nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.label: Historical probability of being the game's top scorer by team scoring rank and usage gap
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.measurement: From 5 seasons of box scores compute for every player-game his rank among teammates by pregame expected points, the gap to the top rival in expected points, minutes and the indicator of leading both teams in points (with tie handling set per rule); fit a conditional logit on gap, team scoring concentration and OT; output P(leader) by rank-gap cell with empirical-Bayes shrinkage (prior weight 80 games per cell).
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.mechanism: The leader is the maximum of about 20 players' points, concentrated among each team's top two or three scorers; the share a player has as leader depends on the gap in expected points to the nearest rivals, not on his own mean.
nba.leader_share_by_usage_rank.rationale: Treating each player's points as independent normals overstates the chance of the second option and ignores that teammates' points are negatively correlated given team total; empirical leader shares by rank and gap calibrate the max-of-correlated-variables model.
raw_data: player-game points, minutes, team and opponent identifiers

nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.label: League-wide probability of extreme single-game events over the remaining regular season (325+ combined points, 15+ steals plus blocks)
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.measurement: Game total: for each remaining game, regulation total = mean from both teams' opponent-adjusted pace and offensive ratings as of the game date plus an empirical residual with a generalised-Pareto tail above the 99th percentile (5 seasons); add overtime periods and combined OT points from nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin; P(total >= 325) by simulation. Steals plus blocks: per player-game, a bivariate negative binomial from shrunk per-36 rates (prior weight 1,000 minutes) times projected minutes, tail checked against 20 seasons of single-game maxima; P(any player >= 15) = 1 - product over player-games. Season probability = 1 - product over remaining games, Cup knockout games included and the Cup final excluded. As-of: nightly.
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.mechanism: 'Any game' and 'any player' contracts are unions over all remaining games of rare events whose per-game probability depends on both teams' pace and offense plus overtime periods (game totals) or on a few high-activity defenders (combined steals and blocks), so the season probability is 1 minus the product over games of (1 - p_g).
nba.league_extreme_game_event_rate.rationale: These events sit far in the tail: a 325-point game needs exceptional pace and shooting and usually more than one overtime, and 15+ steals plus blocks by one player is extremely rare. Per-game probabilities are tiny and governed by tail shape (count of OT periods, heavy-tailed defensive activity), so fits to means can be wrong by orders of magnitude, and the union over about 1,230 games compounds the error.

nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.label: League-wide first-passage race to a single-game scoring threshold (first 50-point game) with same-day ties
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.measurement: For each candidate i and remaining regular-season game g on date t_g: p_ig = P(points >= 50 | plays) from nba.single_game_ceiling_tail (generalised-Pareto exceedance above 35 points with the overtime adjustment) times P(plays g) from the availability inputs. Simulate 20000 seasons in date order: draw hits game by game, stop at the first date with any hit and split 1/N among same-date hitters. Candidates: players projected at 20+ points per game or with a 45+ game in the last 2 seasons; all others enter as a residual field with a league-wide per-game rate fitted on 10 seasons. As-of: nightly; resolved once a 50-point game occurs.
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.mechanism: The first 50-point game of the season is a race across all high-volume scorers: every game a candidate plays carries a small probability of 50+, and the winner is the candidate whose hit comes on the earliest calendar day, with same-day hits splitting the payout.
nba.league_first_to_threshold_race.rationale: A per-player 'scores 50 this season' probability is not the contract: the price depends on how many rival candidates exist, how early each plays and how often, and on same-day splits. Subtle: the race is usually decided in the first weeks or months, so early-season schedule density, minutes restrictions after the preseason and the number of credible candidates matter more than full-season rates.

nba.leg_void_state.label: Leg void-state probabilities and combo payoff rule
nba.leg_void_state.measurement: For each leg: P(void) = P(inactive) + P(protected early exit) + P(postponement beyond 48 hours) from the availability model; compute joint outcome probabilities for each void combination; apply the contract's rule (void whole, drop leg, or No) to compute the payoff probability; the rule is an input to be read from rules_primary when a combo series is live.
nba.leg_void_state.mechanism: The combination's payoff depends on how a void leg (inactive player, protected early exit, postponement) is treated.
nba.leg_void_state.rationale: If one leg can void, the effective probability of Yes given not void differs from the product of the remaining legs, and the void probability itself is correlated with other legs through the injury event.
