nba.lineup_adj_rating.label: Availability-adjusted team rating for tonight's active set
nba.lineup_adj_rating.measurement: Sum over expected-minute allocation of per-player impact (RAPM/EPM/BPM shrunk) for the active set vs team average-active baseline; difference gives point-spread adjustment; validate with with/without team splits when sample allows.
nba.lineup_adj_rating.mechanism: Team strength given who is actually active, computed by summing player impact over expected minutes, moves spreads, totals and every player prop in the game.
nba.lineup_adj_rating.rationale: A star absence changes team net rating by an amount far larger than most other features; the market reprices within minutes of the report. The model needs an independent player-impact valuation to avoid just reading the market. Subtle: impact of replacing a player is not the star's full value (usage redistributes), and replacement is nonlinear when multiple players are out.

nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.label: Lineup-conditional per-100 rates for points, rebounds and assists
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.measurement: Per player: per-100-possession PTS, REB, AST computed by on-court partner set (with/without each of the top-3 teammates by minutes), minimum 300 possessions per cell, empirical-Bayes shrinkage toward the player's overall rate with k=400 possessions; applied to tonight's expected lineup from the confirmed or projected starters; as-of = latest lineup information.
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.mechanism: The three components move differently when teammates are on or off court: a creator off court raises the player's usage and assists, a big off court raises rebounds.
nba.lineup_conditional_component_rates.rationale: Season-average per-minute rates blur lineup regimes, and teammate_absence_shift is a single directional signal; separate rates per partner set are needed for a sum that moves in offsetting directions.

nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.label: Opponent live-ball turnover rate and primary handler carelessness
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.measurement: From play-by-play classify opponent turnovers as live-ball (steal-credited or bad-pass) or dead-ball; compute live-ball turnovers per 100 possessions for the opponent over last 40 games (half-life 20), shrink to league mean with prior weight 20 games; add the turnover rate of the expected primary ball handlers (from lineup) and adjust for opponent's pace. As-of: injury report.
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.mechanism: Steals mostly come from live-ball turnovers (bad passes, dribbles stripped); the opponent's rate of live-ball versus dead-ball turnovers and the quality of its primary handlers set steal supply.
nba.live_ball_turnover_profile.rationale: Total opponent turnovers per game include offensive fouls, shot-clock and out-of-bounds events that cannot be stolen; the live-ball share and the primary handler's turnover rate are the supply for the steal contract.
raw_data: PBP turnover types, steal credit, lineups

nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.label: Distribution of the league-longest win streak and the number of tied teams (1/N payout) from game-level simulation
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.measurement: Simulate 20000 seasons from nba.standings_sim: draw team ratings from the posterior (rating uncertainty common across a team's games), form each game's win probability from rating difference, home court and rest, then record each team's longest run (a streak carrying over the Cup group stage and counting Cup knockout games before the final, excluding the final, play-in and playoffs). For each team report P(team has the strict maximum), P(team is in the tied set), the distribution of N and E[payout] = E[floor(100/N)/100 * 1{team in the tied set}]. Calibrate the serial dependence by comparing simulated run-length distributions with the last 15 seasons of real streak lengths (league-longest streak and its tie frequency). As-of: games completed to date, with the current run for each team carried in.
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.mechanism: The league-longest streak is the maximum over 30 teams of the longest run of consecutive wins in each team's sequence, so a 'longest streak' contract depends on every team's game-by-game win probabilities, their serial dependence, and the chance that two or more teams share the maximum and split the payout.
nba.longest_streak_max_and_tie_model.rationale: KXNBATEAMWINSTREAK pays $1/N to each of N teams tied for the longest streak and only regular-season games (Cup games before the final included) count, so the value for one team is P(it holds the maximum) times E[1/N | it does]. Strengths matter through a convex path: the best team is not only more likely to have a long run but also faces a different set of opponents and rest games, and common rating shocks make streaks cluster in time and in teams. Ignoring ties overstates the value of a favourite when two strong teams reach the same length.

nba.margin_decay_after_pull.label: Margin decay after starters are pulled (by coach and lead size)
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.measurement: From play-by-play: margin at the time both starters of the leading team are out and the final margin; compute mean and sd of the change by lead bucket (10-14, 15-19, 20+) and by coach with 3 seasons of data, shrunk to league with k=8 games; as-of the last completed game; output drift and sd for tonight's coaches.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.mechanism: The final margin equals the margin at the pull time plus a bench-vs-bench drift whose size depends on lead and coach.
nba.margin_decay_after_pull.rationale: Blowout probability alone does not tell how much a 20-point lead at 6:00 shrinks; a coach who pulls starters early gives up points.

nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.label: Pace- and total-dependent margin standard deviation (own-model, not line-based)
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.measurement: Fit sd_margin = a + b × sqrt(own-model possessions) + c × |own-model mean margin| on 5 seasons of team-games (own predictions, not closing lines); report quantile curves (10/25/50/75/90) with a skew parameter for heavy favourites; validate by the probability integral transform per bucket.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.mechanism: Margin variance scales with possession count and total scoring, and with spread through garbage time.
nba.margin_heteroscedasticity.rationale: The existing score_resid is defined around lines, which is market-derived; the variance should come from the game's own pace/total estimates so that cover probabilities at wide spreads are correct.

nba.midgame_exit_hazard.label: In-game early-exit hazard (injury, ejection, foul-out, minutes cap)
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.measurement: From play-by-play, per player-season count games with >=1 minute where minutes < 0.55 x pregame-expected minutes and the exit was not a blowout rest (margin<15 at exit) divided by games entered; classify cause by sub-in/sub-out and injury report. Combine as hazard per 36 minutes with beta(2,40) prior shrinkage and a status multiplier (probable/questionable-return/minutes-restricted) estimated from historical status vintages. As-of: injury report at the latest vintage before tip.
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.mechanism: Once a player enters the game the contract settles on his stats even if he plays 5 minutes, so truncation by an early exit converts directly into NO.
nba.midgame_exit_hazard.rationale: The rules void only players who are inactive or never take the court; an injury exit after 6 minutes settles NO at near-certainty. The hazard is player-specific (age, injury history, listed status, foul rate) and is distinct from planned blowout minutes cuts.

nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.label: Minutes scenario mixture weights and component rates
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.measurement: From 3+ seasons of play-by-play, classify each player-game into regimes by the minutes and score margin (blowout: |margin|>=18 with 4th-quarter minutes<8; foul-limited: >=4 fouls by Q3; OT; restriction: coach-announced); fit regime weights as a multinomial logit of (own-model spread, rest, opponent pace, bench depth) with ridge shrinkage; each regime's stat-per-minute rates estimated with 15-game half-life and a prior from players of the same role; as-of timestamp = last injury report vintage.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.mechanism: Minutes are a mixture of regimes (blowout truncation, normal, foul-limited, OT, restricted) whose weights depend on game state and each regime has different per-minute stat rates.
nba.minutes_scenario_mixture.rationale: The existing nba.minutes is a point projection that hides the multimodality; for a threshold sum, P(S>=25) is driven by the weight of the full-minutes regime, not by the mean minutes.

nba.monthly_window_schedule.label: Games-in-window and schedule for monthly awards
nba.monthly_window_schedule.measurement: games_in_window per candidate team from the league schedule; expected counting stats = per-game mean x games with 10-game shrinkage; probability of winning within conference = softmax over candidates of standardized (points, wins, efficiency) with temperature fit on past months; update on the as-of date.
nba.monthly_window_schedule.mechanism: Monthly player/rookie/coach/defender awards depend on games played inside the window, with fewer games for a candidate lowering his total counting stats and chance of an extreme month.
nba.monthly_window_schedule.rationale: Players on teams with 12 games in the window versus 16 have different expected volume; the conference split of winners and ties matters for pro-rata payout.

nba.multi_game_ml_pack_model.label: Multi-game moneyline pack joint probability
nba.multi_game_ml_pack_model.measurement: For each leg compute P(win) from the own game model (availability-adjusted net rating difference + home court + rest, margin sd about 12, normal CDF at zero including the OT split); joint = product of leg probabilities; test residual cross-game dependence by comparing realised pack hit rates with products over 10 seasons of same-day game pairs (expect correlation near zero); propagate leg-probability uncertainty (posterior sd per leg) to an interval on the product; as-of: a single snapshot time for all legs.
nba.multi_game_ml_pack_model.mechanism: An all-legs-win pack over separate games is the product of per-game win probabilities with a small correction for shared same-slate information.
nba.multi_game_ml_pack_model.rationale: KXNBAPREPACK2ML/3ML settle Yes only if every named team wins; with legs in different games, independence is nearly right, but leg errors compound multiplicatively and late same-day injury news can hit several legs' information sets at once, so the legs must be priced on one consistent as-of snapshot.

nba.next_contract_value_model.label: Next-contract value distribution (maximum and minimum tiers, Bird rights, comparables)
nba.next_contract_value_model.measurement: For the named player compute his maximum tier from years of service (recalled 25/30/35% of the cap and the designated-veteran criteria, to be checked) and the projected cap for the signing season from the league's published projection; model value as a share of the cap with a censored (Tobit) regression at the max and the minimum on age, prior two-season impact (box plus-minus type metric), minutes, All-NBA status and position, fitted on the last 6 free-agency and extension classes; years and annual value modelled jointly; simulate destination with nba.player_move_destination_model to apply cap-space feasibility. As-of: the market timestamp, updated on reported negotiations.
nba.next_contract_value_model.mechanism: A player's next contract is bounded by the CBA's maximum tiers (a percentage of the cap by years of service) and minimums, and within that range set by comparable deals, his impact and age, and the cap space of teams that want him, with Bird rights letting the incumbent team exceed the cap.
nba.next_contract_value_model.rationale: KXNBANEXTCONTRACT is a contract-size market kept under this key by the reconciliation, and no other input here produces a value distribution. Many star contracts sit exactly at the maximum, so the distribution has a point mass at the tier cap (a strike just below the max is near certain for a max-level player); the projected cap for the signing season moves the dollar value of the max, and extensions versus free agency have different ceilings.

nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.label: Non-additive multi-absence cost curve
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.measurement: Fit on 5 seasons of team-games: margin residual vs number of missing rotation players (top-8 by minutes) and the sum of their impact values, with spline in missing impact and interaction with depth index (average impact of players 9-12); predictions per scenario branch; shrink spline with ridge; as-of nightly after injury report.
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.mechanism: The margin cost of losing several rotation players is not the sum of individual costs because the replacement pool deteriorates and rotations compress.
nba.nonadditive_absence_curve.rationale: The existing catalog sums per-player impact (player_impact, lineup_adj_rating) but missing two starters on a team with a deep bench costs less than two times one, whereas on a thin team it costs more; the curve must be estimated by roster depth.

nba.on_court_assist_share.label: On-court assist share of team assisted field goals
nba.on_court_assist_share.measurement: Share = player AST / (team assisted FGM while player on court), computed over last 60 games with half-life 25 games, separately for lineups with and without the top co-creator; shrink to role prior with k=300 on-court team assisted FGM; projected AST = share × expected team assisted FGM in projected minutes; as-of last game.
nba.on_court_assist_share.mechanism: The fraction of the team's assisted makes credited to the player while he is on the floor, which is the stable per-opportunity rate.
nba.on_court_assist_share.rationale: Potential assists and usage are indirect; the on-court assist share is the direct outcome rate, decomposed by lineup and whether co-creators are present, and is the cleanest basis for projecting the count from team assisted makes.
raw_data: play-by-play with assist credit and lineups

nba.opening_night_starter_signals.label: Opening-night starter signals (camp lineups, preseason starts, coach statements)
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.measurement: Score for each player = 0.5 x indicator of starting both of the last 2 preseason games + 0.3 x last season's start share + 0.2 x coach statement (coded 0/0.5/1); map to probability via logistic fit on 8 seasons of opener starters; set to 0 if the status is out or doubtful; combine with injury probability; as-of 24 hours before the opener and again at confirmation.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.mechanism: The first regular-season game's starting five is predicted from the preseason starting lineups, camp reports and coach statements, with strong incumbency.
nba.opening_night_starter_signals.rationale: A season-opener market has no in-season history, so the signal is the preseason; the team's preseason starters in the final two preseason games are usually the opener's starters, but not always.
raw_data: preseason starter flags, coach statement coding

nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.label: Starting-five first-stint offensive and defensive rating and scoring-event mix
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.measurement: For each team compute points per 100 possessions and per-possession scoring-event distribution (0,1,2,3 points) for the first 8 minutes of games using the modal starting five over last 60 games (half-life 30 games), shrink to the team's full-game rating with prior weight 400 possessions; when tonight's starters differ, recompute via player-level on/off ridge ratings. As-of: starters confirmation time.
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.mechanism: The race is decided in the first 4-8 minutes by the starters, whose joint rating differs from season team rating and depends on the exact five.
nba.opening_stint_unit_rating.rationale: Season team ratings average starters and bench; a starter-specific, first-stint rating (with set plays, shot mix and turnover rate) is the relevant strength and changes immediately if one starter is replaced.
raw_data: lineup stints in first period with possessions and points

nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.label: Opponent's rate of open and wide-open three-point attempts allowed (closeout quality)
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.measurement: From team-level aggregate defense dashboards (closest-defender bins, one row per team and date window, not per-shot; window set by a DateTo filter to games before tip) compute per defense the percentage of opponent threes taken with closest defender >= 4 ft (wide open) and 2-4 ft (open), the corner share allowed, and opponent 3PA allowed per 100 possessions; 60-game half-life, shrink to league mean with prior weight 40 games; match against the shooter's tonight's expected cell mix.
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.mechanism: A defense's effect on a shooter's threes shows up in the proportion of attempts that are open, which is a scheme trait and more persistent than opponent 3P% allowed.
nba.opp_three_openness_allowed.rationale: Opponent 3P% allowed mixes luck with scheme; the open-attempt share allowed and the opponent's volume allowed by shot type are stable within a season and map directly to a shooter's catch-and-shoot context.
raw_data: team defense shot dashboard: attempts by defender distance

nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.label: Final-margin pmf conditional on overtime
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.measurement: Empirical pmf of |final margin| for games with OT_periods = 1, 2, 3+ over 15 seasons; fit folded-normal with sd s_OT estimated by maximum likelihood (about 6-7 for one OT); combine with P(OT) from the tie model: P(band) = P(reg in band)(1-P(OT)) + P(OT) × P(OT margin in band).
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.mechanism: If regulation ties, the final margin is the margin of a five-minute period (or more), concentrated in 1-8 points.
nba.ot_final_margin_pmf.rationale: Mass of the lowest bands is the sum of a regulation part and an OT part; the OT part follows a different distribution with folded structure.

nba.ot_period_distribution.label: Distribution of number of overtime periods and OT scoring
nba.ot_period_distribution.measurement: Empirical P(k OT periods) from 15 seasons: P(1), P(2), P(3+) conditional on OT; per-period points per team sampled from the league distribution adjusted for pace (mean about 11-12 per team per 5 minutes, sd 5); update yearly; for series OT: P(at least one OT game) = sum over series length L of P(L) * (1 - prod over games g of (1 - p_g)), with P(L) from nba.series_model (4-7 games, shorter for mismatched teams) and p_g from nba.reg_tie_pmf_model using each game's own-model margin; inflate the variance across games because closeness is positively correlated within a series (estimate by the observed share of series with >=1 OT game versus the independent prediction on 15 seasons of playoff series). The settled quantity (at least one OT game, or a count) is unsampled, see u6.
nba.ot_period_distribution.mechanism: If overtime occurs, additional periods occur with a small probability and each period adds a fixed block of minutes and points.
nba.ot_period_distribution.rationale: The count of OT periods matters for series OT markets and for strike markets on total, bench or team stats within the family; the draft treats OT as one event.

nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.label: Market-free overtime probability and overtime scoring increment from the ratings-implied regulation margin
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.measurement: Step 1: regulation-margin mean mu from step 1 of nba.rating_blowout_minutes_curve (opponent-adjusted net ratings x expected possessions/100 + home advantage, as-of tipoff, adjusted for confirmed inactives). Step 2: P(regulation tie) = logistic regression of the indicator 'regulation margin = 0' on |mu| over the last 5 regular seasons (about 6000 games; league base rate roughly 5-7%, to be estimated, not assumed), smoothed across 1-point |mu| bins. Step 3: per-team OT points = league points per team per OT period from play-by-play (roughly 11-13, to be estimated) scaled by the team's opponent-adjusted pace and offensive rating relative to league; combined OT points = sum over both teams. Step 4: P(k-th OT | (k-1)-th OT) = pooled empirical tie rate of five-minute periods with prior weight 200 OT periods. Output: P(OT), P(2+ OT), per-team and combined OT-points distributions. No spread, total or other price enters; the closing line is used only to benchmark calibration.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.mechanism: A game goes to overtime only if the regulation margin is exactly zero, so P(OT) is the mass at zero of the regulation-margin distribution, highest for evenly matched teams; each five-minute overtime then adds scoring at both teams' per-minute rates, and a further overtime follows with the tie probability of a five-minute period.
nba.ot_prob_ratings_margin.rationale: The catalog nba.ot_model conditions P(OT) on the closing-spread bucket (a market quantity) and says one OT adds about 10-12 points to totals, which is the per-team figure, not the combined one. A market-free version takes the regulation-margin distribution from team ratings and sizes OT correctly: roughly 11-13 points per team and 22-26 combined per period, with repeated overtimes possible. Subtle: the zero-margin mass is larger than a continuous normal approximation gives, because end-of-game tactics (holding for the last shot, fouling when ahead by three) cluster regulation margins between 0 and 3.

nba.overseas_signing_hazard.label: Overseas (CBA) signing hazard for unsigned NBA players
nba.overseas_signing_hazard.measurement: Reference class of former NBA rotation players aged 27+ unsigned by training camp 2010-2026 and the share signing in the CBA within 12 months; logistic on age, last-season minutes, injury status, prior overseas history and NBA minimum-offer reports; multiply by window coverage of CBA registration periods; as-of: market snapshot.
nba.overseas_signing_hazard.mechanism: An unsigned or fringe NBA player signs in the CBA when NBA offers are at or below the minimum and a CBA club offers more, subject to foreign-player slots and registration windows.
nba.overseas_signing_hazard.rationale: KXNBATOJOINCBA counts only an official CBA club announcement or league registration; the decision depends on the player's NBA market and health, not on rumours, and on CBA calendar windows, so the hazard is concentrated before the CBA season.

nba.own_game_environment.label: Own-model game environment (team points, possessions)
nba.own_game_environment.measurement: Team points = pace_own x (opponent-adjusted ORtg) / 100 using 20-game exponentially weighted ratings with opponent adjustment by ridge (lambda tuned on 2 prior seasons); possessions = geometric mean of the two teams' opponent-adjusted pace; adjustment for tonight's active set via lineup rating deltas; output team points and sd.
nba.own_game_environment.mechanism: Both teams' scoring environment determines how many scoring chances exist in the minutes played.
nba.own_game_environment.rationale: nba.implied_team_totals is derived from the sportsbook spread and total, which is market-derived, so it should be a benchmark; an own estimate from ratings and pace gives an independent environment.

nba.own_model_team_totals.label: Own-model expected team points and total (market-free shared scoring factor)
nba.own_model_team_totals.measurement: possessions = pace composition of the two teams (nba.pace, lineup-aware, last 20 games weighted with half-life 8 games, shrunk to league mean with k=15 games); points per possession = availability-adjusted offence versus opponent defence rating with home adjustment, shrunk with k=20 games; team points = possessions x ppp; residual sd by team from own predictions on 5 seasons (not closing lines); output joint (margin, total) mean and covariance for the simulation.
nba.own_model_team_totals.mechanism: Expected team points = expected game possessions times availability-adjusted points per possession against the specific opponent, with a residual distribution built from own predictions; gives the shared scoring factor that same-game legs load on.
nba.own_model_team_totals.rationale: The shared pace/total factor must come from an own-model team total because a total implied by sportsbook lines is a market output and cannot serve as an input; this input also supplies the margin-total residual correlation that sportsbook-implied totals cannot.

nba.pace.label: Pace/possessions, opponent-adjusted, lineup-aware
nba.pace.measurement: Regress per-game possessions on team-offense and team-defense pace effects (or compute expected pace = league + (paceA - lg) + (paceB - lg)); filter to competitive minutes; lineup-adjust using on/off pace; compare to market implied total via possessions x efficiency.
nba.pace.mechanism: Possessions per game scale every counting stat and the total; the game's pace is a joint outcome of both teams' preferences and the lineups on the floor.
nba.pace.rationale: Pace is not additive: expected game pace is roughly league average plus each team's deviation, but slower teams usually win the tempo contest on defense and transition-heavy teams are constrained by opponent make-rates. Lineup changes (a primary ball-pusher out) shift pace. Blowouts and intentional fouling alter late possession counts.

nba.pair_difference_correlation.label: Pair-type correlation of player stat residuals
nba.pair_difference_correlation.measurement: For stat s and pair type, compute the correlation of residuals (after removing player and opponent effects and minutes) over 5 seasons for pairs of similar roles; pool in role-pair cells with shrinkage k=60 games; report the correlation and the implied variance of the difference var = var_A + var_B - 2 rho sd_A sd_B; produce P(A > B), P(tie), P(B > A) via a bivariate negative-binomial.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.mechanism: The correlation between two players' counts differs by pair type (teammates, opponents, separate games) and by stat.
nba.pair_difference_correlation.rationale: The draft says positive correlation through game script, but for teammates the allocation effect is negative; a single sign misprices the difference variance and tie mass.
raw_data: player-game stats with team and opponent

nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.label: Rebound percentage conditional on specific frontcourt pairings (ridge on/off)
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.measurement: From stint data, regress player TRB% on indicator vectors of teammates on court (ridge, lambda chosen by rolling-origin CV on previous season, minimum 150 possessions per pair) with opponent offensive-rebounding strength as a covariate; project tonight's stint mix = rotation minutes by lineup weighted by injury-conditioned availability; output expected share and its standard error. DREB% and OREB% estimated separately because OREB is lineup-sensitive.
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.mechanism: A big's share of available boards depends on which other rebounders share the floor in each stint; the same player has very different shares beside a stretch four vs a second center.
nba.pairing_adjusted_reb_share.rationale: Season TRB% averages over pairings; because rotation patterns change with injury news, what matters is the expected minute-weighted mix of tonight's pairings, which is predictable pregame once availability is known.
raw_data: lineup stints: possessions, player oreb/dreb, opp misses while on court

nba.payout_schedule_operator.label: Payout schedule operator g(K) parsed from rules text
nba.payout_schedule_operator.measurement: Implement the two live schedules exactly: points g(s) = floor(10000 x (y/50)^3)/10000 with y = min(50, max(0, 2 x floor(s/2))); threes g(s) = floor(10000 x (y/10)^3)/10000 with y = min(10, s); parse any new schedule from rules_primary/rules_secondary into (band_lo, band_hi, payout) arrays and cap/void fields and check monotonicity against the formula; value = sum over k of P(K=k) g(k); compute sensitivity of value to mean, variance and P(K >= cap) by finite differences; version the parser by rules hash and flag unparsed tables.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.mechanism: The contract's value is E[g(K)] where g is the payout table in the rules text, so the schedule is part of the model.
nba.payout_schedule_operator.rationale: The cubic schedule means value is dominated by the upper tail: for threes with mean 3 the payout at the mean is $0.027, but the expected payout is much higher because 5+ made threes pay $0.125 or more. The operator must therefore be part of the model, not a post-hoc transform.

nba.period_foul_bonus_state.label: Team-foul and bonus-state exposure per period (foul reset each quarter, end-of-period fouling)
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.measurement: Compute team FTA per quarter and fouls per quarter from play-by-play over 2 seasons with 60-game half-life; estimate crew and team coefficients on quarter FTA via mixed model; project expected time-to-bonus in each quarter and expected FTA by period for tonight's matchup and crew; output expected FT points by period. As-of: crew assignment (announced game day) and team rates.
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.mechanism: Team fouls reset each quarter, so the shape of free-throw production within a period depends on when a team reaches the penalty, and Q4 end-of-period fouling adds free throws that distort Q4 totals and margins.
nba.period_foul_bonus_state.rationale: Free-throw volume per period differs from per-game rates because bonus onset is quarter-specific; crews that call more early fouls bring forward bonus situations in Q1/Q3, which can change period totals by 2-3 points; the effect is partly predictable from crew and team foul rates.
raw_data: PBP fouls and FTA by period

nba.period_margin_pmf.label: Empirical period-margin and period-total probability mass functions (ties, half-point cut points)
nba.period_margin_pmf.measurement: From all games in 5 seasons compute standardized period margin and total (actual minus rating-based expectation, built without market lines), fit a discrete mixture (Skellam-like with pace-dependent variance and a small-excess-kurtosis component) per period type (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, 1H, 2H-with-OT) via maximum likelihood with a team-pair variance covariate; report pmf at integer margins within +/-25 and the tie probability by expected pace tercile.
nba.period_margin_pmf.mechanism: Quarter margins are small integers with a sizeable mass at zero and at +/-1..3; winner, spread and total contracts cut this discrete distribution at specific points, so pmf shape (not only mean and sd) sets the probability.
nba.period_margin_pmf.rationale: A Gaussian approximation misprices tie mass (about 4-6% per quarter) and the probability of exceeding a half-point strike; the shape depends on pace (lower-possession periods have fewer scoring events) and on variance of the team-pair.
raw_data: linescore by period for each game incl. OT points

nba.period_possession_split.label: Possessions by quarter and team pace profile (fast early, slower late in lopsided games)
nba.period_possession_split.measurement: From play-by-play compute possessions per quarter per team with the standard possession formula (FGA - OREB + TOV + 0.44 FTA) by period for the last 2 seasons with 50-game half-life; model matchup period pace as weighted geometric mean with a slow-team weight of about 0.55 (estimate by regression); condition Q4 on pregame blowout-probability tercile. Output expected possessions per period and sd.
nba.period_possession_split.mechanism: Possessions per quarter vary by period (fast Q1, slower Q4 in decided games) and each coach has a pace style, so period totals scale with a period-specific possession count.
nba.period_possession_split.rationale: Applying game pace to a quarter overstates Q4 possessions in blowouts and understates Q1 for fast starters; the possession count times PPP is the correct decomposition for totals and team totals.

nba.play_in_path_model.label: Play-in bracket path probabilities given pre-play-in seed and relative strength
nba.play_in_path_model.measurement: Encode the bracket (7v8 winner gets the 7 seed; 9v10 loser is out; loser of 7v8 plays winner of 9v10 for the 8 seed), compute per-game win probabilities with home-court from team ratings and rest, and convolve to P(final seed 7, 8, out | pre-play-in seed, opponents); estimate the distribution of opponents from the standings simulation. As-of: nightly; rules versioned by season.
nba.play_in_path_model.mechanism: The play-in tournament maps seeds 7-10 to final seeds 7 and 8 through a fixed bracket, so the playoff qualification and the post-play-in seed differ from the regular-season seed; Kalshi's seed contracts are measured before the play-in.
nba.play_in_path_model.rationale: KXNBASEEDOU resolves on the regular-season seed before the play-in while qualification/play-in series depend on play-in outcomes; the same team has different probabilities for 'seed 8 or better' depending on which definition applies.
raw_data: standings and seeds before the Play-In

nba.player_move_destination_model.label: Player destination choice model with cap feasibility
nba.player_move_destination_model.measurement: For each candidate team compute feasibility (cap space or matching salaries within apron rules), asset fit and need (position gap, win-now vs rebuild); estimate a multinomial logit on 10 seasons of moves with these features plus player-preference flags (stated preference, agent reports); add a catch-all with probability from age and contract status; as-of nightly.
nba.player_move_destination_model.mechanism: Destination is a choice among feasible teams determined by cap space or matching assets, team need, and player preference.
nba.player_move_destination_model.rationale: A multi-outcome next-team market needs a distribution over teams; relying on rumor misses cap constraints that exclude most teams.
raw_data: team payroll and cap state, historical moves
